symptom: Rapid successive commits repeatedly cancelled long-running OCI validation before it could complete.
root_cause: Execution optimized local progress without accounting for workflow concurrency cancel-in-progress semantics.
early_signals: OCI workflow uses concurrency with cancel-in-progress for pull_request events
Multiple prior OCI runs were cancelled after newer commits landed
human_cost: No operator intervention; validation latency increased and security evidence was delayed.
prevention_rule: When a long-running acceptance gate is required for objective closure, freeze branch writes until that gate completes unless a new commit is necessary to repair that gate.
automated_detection: Detect repeated cancelled required workflows on successive head SHAs and classify branch-write churn as execution drift.
